summary: Paul David Numrich is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who earned his doctorate from the University of Michigan in 1992. In 2006, he held posts at Loyola University Chicago and the Theological Consortium of Greater Columbus.

Paul Debes was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Nyanatiloka Mahathera from 1931 to 1932. He founded the Buddhistisches Seminar (1948), the journal Wissen und Wandel (1955), and served as a board member of the Buddhistische Gesellschaft Hamburg (1954).

Paul Demiéville was a sinologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Lévi, Chavannes, Meillet, and Pelliot. He held posts at Xiamen University, the Maison Franco-Japonaise, INALCO, EPHE, and was Chair of Chinese Language and Literature at Collège de France (1946–1964).

Paul Deussen was an Indologist and philosopher who completed his habilitation under Eduard Zeller at Humboldt University of Berlin, where he taught as Privatdocent (1881–1887). He taught Sanskrit at the University of Geneva (~1870–1872) and became a professor at Kiel University in 1889.

Paul Dundas was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied under Michael Coulson and at the University of Edinburgh. He led Asian studies at the University of Edinburgh (~1976–2023) and also led the Pali Text Society.

Paul E. Muller-Ortega is a scholar in Indology and religious studies who completed his doctoral studies at the University of California, Santa Barbara. By 2000, he was teaching in the Department of Religion and Classics at the University of Rochester.
Paul Ekman studied at New York University (~1952–1954) and Adelphi University (~1954–1958). He subsequently held a post at the University of California, San Francisco (~1972–2004).

Paul F. Knitter is a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies who studied at the Pontifical Gregorian University and the University of Marburg (~1970–1972). He later held a post at Union Theological Seminary (~2007).

Paul Fredericq was a historian who earned his doctorate from the University of Liège, where he served as professor (~1879–1884). He later became a professor (1883) and rector (1919) at Ghent University.

Paul Fuller is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who completed his PhD at the University of Bristol under Rupert Gethin and also studied under Paul Dundas. He held lectureships at the University of Sydney, Cardiff University, and taught at the University of Edinburgh.

Paul G. Brewster was an Indologist who studied at Oakland City University and the University of Oklahoma. He held teaching posts at the universities of Tennessee and North Carolina, Shurtleff College, Henderson State University, and Tennessee Technological University (1954).

Paul G. Hackett is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held curatorial and bibliographical posts at the University of Virginia (attested 1994, 2003) and positions at Columbia University (attested 2003, 2016), including Lecturer in Classical Tibetan.

Paul Goldschmidt was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Rudolf von Roth, Albrecht Weber, and completed his PhD under Theodor Benfey at Göttingen. In 1874, he served as an epigraphist and Commissioner of Archaeology for the Government of Ceylon.
Paul Greenough is a scholar of history and Indology who earned his PhD from the University of Chicago (1968–1977). He held a post in history at the University of Iowa beginning in 1974.

Paul Groner is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who earned his PhD from Yale University and studied under Akira Hirakawa at the University of Tokyo. He has served as a religious studies professor at the University of Virginia.

Paul Hacker was an Indologist and philosopher who earned his PhD at Berlin and completed his habilitation under Willibald Kirfel at Bonn. He served as professor at the Mithila Institute (1954–1955), the University of Bonn (1955–1963), and the University of Münster (1963–1978).

Paul Harrison is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology who completed his PhD under Jan Willem de Jong and Tissa Rajapatirana at ANU. He held posts at the University of Canterbury and Stanford University.
Paul Hershman was an Indologist and anthropologist who studied at the London School of Economics (~1971–1975). He served as a Lecturer in Anthropology at the University of Sussex from ~1974 to 1976.
Paul Hoornaert is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who held posts, including lecturer, at Kanazawa University (attested 1991, 2002).

Paul Horn was a scholar of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies who completed his PhD under Christian Bartholomae at Halle-Wittenberg. He served as Privatdozent (1889) and extraordinary professor (1900) at the University of Strasbourg.
